The two persistence targets and how the popover decides between them (packet 4, the Save/`comment-save` vs. `comment-save-feedback` handlers): a TEAM COMMENT (IN-project) is decided by `saveBtn`'s own handler (7959-7972) — it writes `_activeComment.text`/`.resolved` from the DOM (7962-7963), lazily inits `state.comments=[]` if absent (7964), tests membership with `state.comments.indexOf(_activeComment)<0` (7965) — an IDENTITY check against the live object reference, not a value/id comparison — and if not yet present, discards a never-typed-into blank draft outright (`!_activeComment.text.trim()`, 7967, `closeCommentPopover();return;`) or else pushes it (7968); either way (existing or freshly kept) it then calls `saveActiveLayerFrame();closeCommentPopover();updateUI();refreshFbAvatars();` (7970) and a guarded `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` (7971). A DEBUG FEEDBACK entry (OUT-of-project, CLAUDE.md §6) is the SEPARATE `comment-save-feedback` handler (7934-7958): it requires a non-empty note (7940, else a toast and return), reads the blocking checkbox and optional name/email (persisted to `state.userProfile` then `saveUserProfile()`, 7947-7949), and calls `window.SMFeedback.submitFeedback({...})` (7950-7954) — this path NEVER touches `state.comments` at all (confirmed: no `state.comments` reference anywhere in 7934-7958), so a feedback submission never becomes a team comment and vice versa, matching the packet 1 lead-in's own stated invariant (7724-7728). Delete (`delBtn`, 7973-7979) removes by `state.comments.indexOf(_activeComment)` then `.splice` (7975-7976) — the SAME identity-based lookup as Save's own membership test, so Delete only ever removes an entry that is ALREADY in the array (a never-saved draft has no array entry to remove, `idx>=0` guards the no-op case).

The module-level state (`_activeComment`, `_activeFbTags`, `_activeShotDataUrls`, `_recording`, `_recActionMark`/`_recClickMark`/`_recStartTime`, `_recordedActionTrail`/`_recordedClickTrail`) and the exact reset point of each on open/close: `openCommentPopover` (packet 3) resets `_activeFbTags=[]` + every `.fb-tag` button's own `active` class (7870-7871), the blocking checkbox (7872), `_recording`/`_recordedActionTrail`/`_recordedClickTrail` (7873, followed by `updateRecordUI()` 7874 to repaint the record button/status from that cleared state), and the screenshot strip via `setCommentShots(...)` (7877-7878, itself in packet 1) — reading EITHER the new `screenshotDataUrls` array or the old singular `screenshotDataUrl` field for backward compatibility with an entry saved before feedback #208. `closeCommentPopover` (packet 3) resets `_activeComment=null`, the SAME three recording fields (`_recording`/`_recordedActionTrail`/`_recordedClickTrail`, 7886), and calls `setCommentShots([])` (7887) — `_activeFbTags` is deliberately NOT reset on close (only on the NEXT open, 7870), and `_recActionMark`/`_recClickMark`/`_recStartTime` are never reset by either open or close, only ever reassigned by `startRecording` (7820-7822) — stale marks from a previous recording session are harmless since `_recording` itself gates every read of them.

The screenshot strip contract (packet 1 + the wiring in packet 4): accepted inputs are drag&drop (`shotDrop`'s own `drop` listener, 7913-7917, reading `e.dataTransfer.files`), click-to-browse (`shotDrop`'s own `click` listener opens `shotInput.click()`, 7910; `shotInput`'s own `change` listener, 7918-7921, reading `shotInput.files`, a `multiple`-attribute `<input type=file>` per index.html:2102), and Cmd+V paste (`pop`'s own `paste` listener, 7922-7932, reading `e.clipboardData.items`, filtering to `image/*` entries via `.getAsFile()`) — all three funnel into the SAME `loadCommentShotFiles(files)` (packet 1, 7775-7787). MIME filter: `loadCommentShotFiles` itself filters to `f.type.indexOf('image/')===0` (7776); the paste listener applies an EQUIVALENT per-item filter before collecting into `pastedFiles` (7929) so only image clipboard items ever reach `loadCommentShotFiles`. Ordering guarantee: `pending`/`results` (7778) is a pre-sized `Array(imgFiles.length)`, each `FileReader`'s own `onload` writes into `results[i]` at ITS OWN closed-over index `i` (7779-7785, not push order) — so despite `FileReader` being async and files potentially finishing out of order, `results` always ends up in the ORIGINAL pick/drop/paste order once the last one (`--pending===0`) fires `addCommentShots(results)` (7783). Upload happens in feedback-bridge.js at submit time (`uploadScreenshotsIfAny`, CLAUDE.md §6, cited by name only) — this scope only ever holds data URLs in `_activeShotDataUrls`, confirmed: no `fetch`/upload/network call anywhere in 7724-7994.

The recording contract: `startRecording` (packet 2, 7817-7825) reads two marks via `window.SMFeedback.actionLogMark()`/`.clickLogMark()` (7820-7821, feedback-bridge.js:154-155) at Record-click time; `stopRecording` (7826-7832) reads the trails SINCE those marks via `.actionTrailSince(mark)`/`.clickTrailSince(mark)` (7829-7830, feedback-bridge.js:156-157) at Stop-click time. `updateRecordUI` (packet 2, 7797-7816) writes to the DOM: while `_recording` is true, `#comment-record`'s own textContent becomes `SM.t('commentStopRecordBtn')` plus an `.ac` (active) class, and `#comment-record-status` shows `commentRecordingInProgressHint` (7801-7803); once stopped, the button reverts to `commentRecordBtn` text/no `.ac` class (7805-7806), and the status either shows a tallied `'✓ N action(s)/clic(s) enregistré(s)...'` count (`_recordedActionTrail.length + _recordedClickTrail.length`, 7809-7810) if either trail is non-null, or hides entirely (7811-7813) if nothing was ever recorded. The recording flag suppresses dismissal in exactly two places, both cited by line: the outside-click listener's own early return `if(_recording)return;` (7990, packet 4, BEFORE the `pop.contains` containment check — so a click anywhere, including outside the popover, never reaches `closeCommentPopover` while recording) and the debug-feedback Save handler's own `if(_recording)stopRecording();` (7938, packet 4) — a 'forgot to hit Stop' safety net that captures the trail up to the moment of Save rather than silently discarding it; the SAME guard exists on the team-comment Save handler (7961) for the identical reason, even though a team comment never reads the recorded trails at all (they are debug-feedback-only fields).

The placement math of `openCommentPopover` (packet 3, 7843-7861) as pure input→output: given `worldPt` (a Paper.js Point in canvas/world space) and the `#canvas-area` element's own `getBoundingClientRect()` (7845), `view.projectToView(worldPt)` (7846, the one Paper.js call in this scope) converts to view-space pixels; `rawLeft=rect.left+vp.x+12,rawTop=rect.top+vp.y-8` (7847) offsets 12px right / 8px up from the pin itself. The 2026-08-27 clamp fix (7848-7858 lead-in) then clamps BOTH axes into `[margin, window.innerWidth|innerHeight - estW|estH - margin]` with `estW=240,estH=420,margin=8` (7859) — `estW` matches the popover's own fixed CSS width (index.html:2056, `width:240px`); `estH` is a generous static estimate (the popover isn't visible yet at measurement time, so `offsetHeight` would read 0) backed by the CSS's own `max-height:calc(100vh - 24px);overflow-y:auto` as the real safety net for whatever this estimate undershoots. Final `pop.style.left`/`.top` (7860-7861) are the clamped, rounded pixel values — no further layout pass reads `worldPt` again.
